svg.font-family: Noto Sans, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: AuditLens technical architecture
svg.desc: People use a browser workbench or a command line. Both talk to the AuditLens server, which runs six steps: Detect with Slither, Understand with optional AI triage, Trace attack paths, Verify exploits in a Foundry sandbox, Fix and validate patches, and Prove with a hash-chained ledger, reports and re-executable proof bundles.
svg.text: How a smart contract moves through AuditLens: Detect → Understand → Trace → Verify → Fix → Prove. Built on Slither, which is used as-is through its Python API.
frontend/ · plain JS, no build step
Takes uploads and runs the six steps below, in order

g.text: Runs every detector; pulls out each function's facts
Rates how exploitable each finding is: a hypothesis
Links attacker → entry point → call → state change
Fills a fixed test template and runs it in the sandbox
Re-runs the exploit and a normal-use test on the patch
Hash-chains every result; packs sources, tests and
ledger into a bundle anyone can re-run

svg.text: Dashed: same code, runs without the server
by Trail of Bits · the deterministic core
• same contract in, same findings out
used unmodified, through its public Python API
• gets Slither's evidence, answers in JSON
• answer is schema-checked; it can't run code
• no API key → offline rule-based heuristic,
• no network, cleared environment, no secrets
• 120 s timeout, CPU and file-size limits
• tests come from fixed templates; the AI
only fills in parameters, never code
• runs original and patched code side by side
Four kinds of evidence, never mixed
Every finding shows which of these it has, and the ledger records each one separately.

g.text: An opinion on exploitability, with a
confidence. Useful, never treated as proof.

text.tspan: A finding is called proven only when an exploit test reproduced it.
Impact figures come from local test setups, not live chains.

svg.text: The ledger detects edits to recorded evidence; it does not prove the tests were the right ones to write.
